episode_title: Brian Chesky on Founder Mode, Designing Culture, and Running Airbnb
content:
Lenny: Brian, your leadership philosophy at Airbnb has inspired intense debate, especially after Paul Graham's essay on 'Founder Mode'. How do you actually run Airbnb today compared to traditional corporate management advice?

Brian Chesky: For years, experienced executives and board members told me: 'Brian, as the company scales, you need to hire professional managers, empower them, step back, and get out of their way.' That is the conventional 'Manager Mode'. And when we followed that playbook before the pandemic, Airbnb became bloated, fragmented, and slow. We had hundreds of divisional silos, duplicate roadmaps, and products that felt disconnected from each other.

When COVID hit and our business dropped 80% in eight weeks, we threw out the conventional playbook and went back to 'Founder Mode'. What does Founder Mode actually mean? It does not mean micromanaging trivial details for the sake of control. It means being in the details of the things that matter most: product design, brand voice, strategic trade-offs, and quality.

Lenny: What does your weekly product review cadence look like now?

Brian Chesky: We eliminated the traditional GM (General Manager) structure and separate business units. We run Airbnb as one single integrated company with one roadmap. Every Sunday night, I review the entire product roadmap. Every major feature goes through a rigorous design and product review with me and our core design leads before anything ships. If you are a founder or product visionary, your job is to hold the unified mental model of the product. The moment you delegate product intuition to disconnected layers of middle management, the soul of your product dies.

We also use the '11-Star Experience' thought experiment. A 5-star Airbnb experience is getting the keys and the room is clean. A 6-star experience is there's a gift basket waiting for you. A 7-star experience is the host knows you like surfing and leaves a surfboard. An 8-star experience is a limousine picks you up at the airport. An 11-star experience is you land at the airport, there are 5,000 cheering fans, and Elon Musk flies you into space! You'll never build the 11-star experience, but it stretches your imagination so that the 6- and 7-star experience suddenly feels completely achievable.
